questions.question: During which phase of the eukaryotic cell cycle does DNA replication take place, producing identical sister chromatids?

options.text: G1 phase
S phase
G2 phase
M phase

questions.explanation: During the S (Synthesis) phase of interphase, the cell replicates its chromosomal DNA so that each chromosome consists of two identical sister chromatids prior to cell division.

questions.question: What is the primary biological outcome of mitotic cell division (mitosis followed by cytokinesis)?

options.text: Four haploid daughter cells that are genetically distinct from the parent cell
Two diploid daughter cells that are genetically identical to the parent cell
Two haploid gametes ready for fertilization
A single polyploid cell with multiple nuclei

questions.explanation: Mitosis is an equational division in which a diploid (2n) mother cell duplicates and evenly distributes its chromosomes to form two genetically identical diploid (2n) daughter cells.

questions.question: In which stage of mitosis do chromosomes align along the equatorial plane (equatorial plate) of the cell?

options.text: Prophase
Metaphase
Anaphase
Telophase

questions.explanation: During metaphase, the fully formed mitotic spindle aligns the condensed chromosomes along the center or metaphase plate of the cell.

questions.question: Why is the meiotic cell division process fundamentally referred to as a 'reduction division'?

options.text: It reduces the physical size and cytoplasmic volume of daughter cells by 90%
It reduces the chromosome number by half, from diploid (2n) to haploid (n)
It reduces the metabolic rate and ATP synthesis of dividing cells
It reduces the total number of cell cycles an organism can undergo

questions.explanation: Meiosis reduces the chromosome complement from the diploid number (2n) to the haploid number (n) during the formation of gametes, preventing the doubling of chromosomes across generations.

questions.question: Which renowned Ethiopian geneticist and agronomist received the Right Livelihood Award in 1989 for establishing the Plant Genetic Resources Centre and conserving native crop landraces?

options.text: Dr. Aklilu Lemma
Prof. Gebissa Ejeta
Dr. Melaku Worede
Prof. Tilahun Yilma

questions.explanation: Dr. Melaku Worede is renowned for preserving Ethiopia's genetic wealth through community-based landrace conservation and establishing the Plant Genetic Resources Centre in Addis Ababa.

questions.question: How does cytokinesis in dividing plant cells differ fundamentally from cytokinesis in animal cells?

options.text: Plant cells pinch inward via a cleavage furrow, whereas animal cells form a middle lamella
Plant cells synthesize a new cell plate and middle lamella between daughter nuclei, whereas animal cells divide by furrowing and constriction of the cell membrane
Plant cells undergo cytokinesis during G1 phase, whereas animal cells undergo cytokinesis in S phase
Plant cells divide their cytoplasm twice, whereas animal cells omit cytokinesis entirely

questions.explanation: Because plant cells are encased by a rigid cell wall, their cytoplasm cannot pinch off. Instead, a new cell plate and wall (middle lamella) are laid down between daughter cells, whereas animal cells form a cleavage furrow that constricts inward.

questions.question: During which phase of the cell cycle does a cell replenish its energy stores, synthesize proteins required for chromosome manipulation, and duplicate some organelles before entering mitosis?

options.text: G1 phase
S phase
G2 phase
M phase

questions.explanation: During the G2 phase (second gap), the cell replenishes energy reserves, synthesizes proteins necessary for spindle assembly and chromosome movement, and duplicates certain organelles as final preparation for mitosis.

questions.question: What primary genetic event occurs during Prophase I of meiosis that does NOT occur during mitotic prophase?

options.text: Degeneration of the cell membrane and immediate lysis of the cytoplasm
Synapsis of homologous chromosomes and crossing over between non-sister chromatids
Separation of sister chromatids to opposite poles of the spindle
Condensation of chromatin into individual visible chromatids

questions.explanation: In Prophase I of meiosis, homologous chromosomes pair up closely (synapsis) to form tetrads and exchange genetic segments through crossing over, creating new allele combinations that do not occur in mitosis.

questions.question: Why is uncontrolled and unregulated progression through the cell cycle dangerous to a multicellular organism?

options.text: It causes all somatic cells to instantly convert into haploid gametes
It results in excessive, uncontrolled cell proliferation leading to the formation of tumors and cancer
It permanently halts all protein synthesis and ATP generation in the body
It leads to the destruction of the nuclear envelope in non-dividing nerve cells

questions.explanation: When internal regulatory checkpoints of the cell cycle fail, cells divide uncontrollably at high density without responding to normal growth-inhibitory signals, which can lead to tumor growth and cancer.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the behavior of chromosomes during Anaphase I of meiosis?

options.text: Sister chromatids separate as centromeres split, moving as individual chromosomes to opposite poles
Homologous chromosome pairs separate and move toward opposite poles while sister chromatids remain attached at their centromeres
All 46 chromosomes migrate to one pole, leaving the other pole completely empty
Non-homologous chromosomes fuse together at the metaphase plate

questions.explanation: In Anaphase I, the centromeres do not divide; instead, homologous chromosomes of each pair separate and move to opposite poles, halving the chromosome number from diploid to haploid.

questions.question: As a cell grows larger in volume during interphase, which physiological limitation creates the need for the cell to divide?

options.text: The surface area-to-volume ratio decreases, making simple diffusion across the plasma membrane inadequate to support the large volume
The concentration of nuclear DNA increases to toxic levels inside the nucleolus
The cell wall dissolves completely when exposed to elevated cytoplasmic pressure
Mitochondria stop producing ATP once the cell diameter exceeds 5 micrometers

questions.explanation: As cell size increases, cytoplasmic volume expands much faster than the membrane surface area, decreasing the surface area-to-volume ratio and making material exchange by diffusion insufficient to meet metabolic demands.

questions.question: A cell with a diploid chromosome number of 2n = 40 undergoes meiosis. How many daughter cells are produced at the completion of Meiosis I and Meiosis II, and how many chromosomes does each daughter cell contain at these respective stages?

options.text: Meiosis I: 2 cells with 40 chromosomes each; Meiosis II: 4 cells with 40 chromosomes each
Meiosis I: 2 cells with 20 chromosomes each; Meiosis II: 4 cells with 20 chromosomes each
Meiosis I: 4 cells with 20 chromosomes each; Meiosis II: 4 cells with 10 chromosomes each
Meiosis I: 2 cells with 10 chromosomes each; Meiosis II: 4 cells with 5 chromosomes each

questions.explanation: Meiosis I is a reduction division that produces 2 haploid cells, each containing 20 duplicated chromosomes (n = 20). Meiosis II separates sister chromatids without altering chromosome number, resulting in 4 haploid daughter cells, each with 20 chromosomes.

questions.question: If a dividing cell is treated with a pharmacological agent that specifically prevents the breakdown of cohesin proteins at the centromeres, at which stage of mitosis will the cell division be arrested?

options.text: Transition from Prophase to Metaphase
Transition from Metaphase to Anaphase
Transition from Telophase to Cytokinesis
Entry from G2 phase into M phase

questions.explanation: During anaphase, cohesin proteins that hold sister chromatids together at the centromere must be cleaved to allow chromatids to separate and move toward opposite poles. Preventing cohesin breakdown arrests the cell at metaphase.

questions.question: In what specific way is Meiosis II mechanistically similar to standard mitotic division, distinguishing it from Meiosis I?

options.text: Both involve the pairing of homologous chromosomes into bivalents
Both involve the separation of individual sister chromatids as centromeres divide
Both are preceded by a complete round of chromosome duplication during S phase
Both reduce the overall ploidy level of daughter cells from 2n to n

questions.explanation: Meiosis II is an equational division analogous to mitosis: chromosomes align individually at the metaphase plate and sister chromatids are pulled to opposite poles upon centromere division, unlike Meiosis I where homologous pairs separate.

questions.question: Which of the following explains why Dr. Melaku Worede's on-farm landrace conservation strategy in Ethiopia proved more sustainable for resource-poor farmers than relying exclusively on imported high-input seeds?

options.text: Native seed landraces were genetically cloned in laboratories to eliminate all phenotypic variation
Locally adapted native seeds possessed broad genetic diversity that provided resilience against drought and pests while outyielding high-input varieties without costly chemical fertilizers
Native landraces were modified to reproduce exclusively by asexual budding rather than sexual pollination
Imported high-input seeds were incapable of germinating in tropical African day-lengths

questions.explanation: Dr. Melaku Worede demonstrated that diverse, locally adapted farmer landraces (such as indigenous durum wheat) could yield 10-15% more than high-input varieties and 20-25% more than original cultivars under local farming conditions without requiring expensive commercial fertilizers or pesticides.
